newsitem.title: USA: figure skating-Skater Baiul asks for alcohol education program.
newsitem.headline: figure skating-Skater Baiul asks for alcohol education program.

text.p: Ukrainian Olympic figure skating champion Oksana Baiul on Monday asked to enroll in an alcohol education programme in an effort to avoid prosecution on drunk driving charges.
Baiul, 19, did not enter a plea during her appearance at a Connecticut court, but instead officially asked to be enrolled in the Pre-Trial Alcohol Education System programme, her lawyer said.
"The programme is in lieu of a plea, and at the end of the programme, the case is expunged from her record," Paul Collins told Reuters.
West Hartford Superior Court Judge Terence Sullivan set Baiul's next court appearance for Feb. 4, when he is expected to rule on whether she has been accepted into the programme.
Baiul's other lawyer, Daniel Blume, told the court his client regretted the Jan. 12 incident, when she ran her Mercedes off a road and crashed.
"She understands the seriousness of this matter," Blume said.
"She understands her conduct could send the wrong message to her millions of friends and fans around the world," he said. "She assures that it will never occur again."
A native of the Ukraine, Baiul shot to fame after she won a gold medal in the 1994 Winter Olympics.

Baiul, who lives in Simsbury, Connecticut, was charged with driving while intoxicated and reckless driving following the accident. She faces a maximum fine of $300 and 30-day suspension of her driver's license on the reckless driving charge.
Police have estimated her speed at 97 mph (156 kph) on a stretch of road where the legal speed limit was 45 mph (72 km), according to court documents.
Baiul suffered a concussion and required stitches. A male passenger received minor injuries.
Baiul, who is two years younger than Connecticut's legal drinking age, had a blood-alcohol content of 0.168 percent at the time of the accident, according to a hospital report that became public.
Connecticut's legal limit for adults is 0.10 percent.
If accepted into the alcohol education programme, Baiul must pay $350 and attend at least eight meetings or counselling sessions, according to a court document.
"It's a programme where they have to go there on a weekly basis and learn about the evils of alcohol," Hartford County Sheriff Walter Kupchunos told reporters.
Baiul, wearing a blue turtleneck sweater and dark stretch pants, did not show any effects of her injuries in court.
She and her lawyers made no comment as they hustled through reporters, cameramen and a small clutch of supporters when leaving the courthouse.
